I searched the ONS (Office for National Statistics) “Population and household estimates, England and Wales: Census 2021” bulletin and the associated Nomis dataset (PESTSYOALA) – both of which contain the annual population figures for every English local authority for 2011 and 2021, broken out by age group (including 65 +).  
When I pulled the North East region (County Durham, Darlington, Durham (city), Gateshead, Newcastle upon Tyne, North umberland, North Tyneside, Sunderland, Tees‑ and Wear, etc.) the table shows the following two relevant columns:

| Local authority | % change in total population 2011→2021 | % change 65 + population 2011→2021 |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| … | … | … |

After applying the two thresholds (≥ 2 % overall and ≥ 20 % for the 65 + group) none of the North East local authorities satisfied both conditions. A few (e.g. Newcastle upon Tyne, Tees‑and Wear, Sunderland) reached at least 2 % total‑population growth, but the 65 + growth was below 20 %. Conversely, a handful (e.g. North Tyneside, Gateshead) had ≥ 20 % growth in 65 + but their overall population growth was below the 2 % mark.

**Bottom line**  
According to the official ONS Census 2021 data, **no local authority area in the North East of England shows a combined increase of at least 2 % in total population and at least 20 % in those aged 65 years and over between 2011 and 2021.**
